content.value_statement: Custom WordPress theme work often spans templates, PHP setup, editor support, styling, and testing. This skill turns that work into a phased workflow for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Breaks WordPress theme work into setup, templates, functions, custom post types, block support, styling, and testing phases.
Lists expected theme files such as templates, assets, includes, language files, and theme support configuration.
Provides copy-paste prompts for invoking related skills during each theme phase.
Defines quality gates for responsive design, accessibility, browser testing, block editor support, and performance.
Connects theme development with frontend, backend, design, Tailwind, Playwright, and WordPress workflows.
limitations: Does not include executable theme source files or reusable starter code.
Depends on other named skills for implementation details and testing execution.
Does not validate generated PHP, JavaScript, or CSS for production security.
Does not cover hosting, deployment, plugin architecture, or WordPress administration.

use_cases.title: Freelance Theme Build
use_cases.description: Freelancers can turn a client design into a theme build checklist with files, templates, and quality gates.

use_cases.title: Agency Project Planning
use_cases.description: Agencies can standardize theme architecture before assigning frontend, backend, and testing tasks.

use_cases.title: Editor Experience Upgrade
use_cases.description: Site owners can plan Gutenberg support, custom blocks, and patterns that improve editing workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Start A Theme
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new theme project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WordPress theme setup plan for [site type]. Include required files, theme header fields, functions.php setup, and enqueue steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build Templates
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the WordPress template hierarchy for [content needs]. List each template file and the content it should render.

prompt_templates.title: Add Block Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan Gutenberg support for this theme. Include theme support flags, block styles, patterns, and editor styling tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Theme Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WordPress theme plan for launch readiness. Check responsive behavior, accessibility, performance, browser coverage, and content editing workflows.

output_examples.input: User asks for a theme setup plan for a nonprofit website.
output: Theme structure with style.css, functions.php, template files, assets, and language folders.
Checklist for menus, thumbnails, RSS support, editor styles, and script enqueueing.
Quality gates for responsive layout, accessibility, and browser testing.

output_examples.input: User asks how to add block editor support to an existing theme.
output_examples.output: A phased plan covering support flags, editor styling, block patterns, custom blocks, and editor testing checkpoints.

best_practices: Review WordPress escaping, sanitization, nonces, and capability checks before using generated PHP.
Use the template hierarchy plan before adding custom files or block behavior.
Test responsive layouts, editor workflows, accessibility, and performance before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not copy generated theme code into production without manual review.
Do not mix plugin behavior into the theme when a plugin is the proper boundary.
Do not skip block editor testing when editors manage page content.

faq.question: Does this skill write a complete WordPress theme?
faq.answer: No. It guides planning and implementation steps. You still need to generate, review, and test the theme code.

faq.question: Can it help with Gutenberg blocks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers block editor support, block styles, patterns, and custom block planning.

faq.question: Does it include WooCommerce work?
faq.answer: Only related workflow references are listed. Use a WooCommerce-specific workflow for store templates and checkout behavior.

faq.question: Is it limited to classic themes?
faq.answer: No. It supports common theme files and Gutenberg planning, but it does not replace WordPress documentation.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What security review is needed for generated code?
faq.answer: Review PHP escaping, nonces, capability checks, dependency sources, and any commands before running or deploying generated code.
